text: Leo was nine, and he was working on a school project about teeth. The lamp over his desk was very bright. "Ouch, my eyes hurt," he said to the smart speaker in the hall. The speaker understood that the light was too strong, so it dimmed the lamp to half. "That's fine now," said Leo. Then he asked, "When does Dr. Moss open on Saturday?" The assistant looked up the dentist's opening hours and said, "Dr. Moss opens at nine on Saturday." Leo wrote the time on his project, next to a drawing of a big tooth. He also asked the assistant to book a visit for his mom at ten. The assistant said the visit was booked and that it would send a reminder the evening before. Leo smiled and went back to his drawing.

They want the phone screen to be less bright.
make the screen dimmer
screen too bright
turn down the brightness
pls lower the brigthness, its blinding me
My eyes hurt when I look at my phone at night. Can you make it softer?
I'm lying in bed and the screen is like a flashlight.
The nurse told me to rest my eyes before sleep, so could you please make the screen a lot darker?
It's so bright by the pool that I can't read anything while the kids swim, so could you change the screen to suit the sun?

A campsite booking keeps a spot for your tent on the nights you choose. Before a trip, people check the dates, how many people are coming, and whether they want a flat place near the water. You usually pay a small fee when you book, and some sites ask you to pay the rest when you arrive. If plans change, people say things like "move my booking to Saturday," "make it three nights instead of two," or "cancel the booking." Many campers also ask for a spot with a table near the tent, because breakfast tastes best outside, with bacon cooked on a small stove until it is crispy.

Person: Can you book me a haircut and tell me when the salon closes today?
Assistant: Sure. Which day and what time would you like the haircut?
Person: Friday morning, around ten. Please ask for someone who is soft with the scissors, my scalp is sensitive.
Assistant: Anna has a free time at ten on Friday. I have booked it. The salon closes at six today.
Person: Thank you. I would like to invite my brother to come along. Can you send him a message?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send messages to other people. I can give you the time and the address to share with him.
Person: That's fine, I'll text him. I have to go and fix the lock on my shed first.

name: check_room_air
does: Reads the air sensor in a room and gives one smooth score from good to bad.
inputs: the name of the room
people say:
- Is the air bad in here?
- It smells stuffy in the bedroom.
- Scan the living room air, please.
- The pollen is awful this April. Is it okay to open the window?
- How clean is the air upstairs?

Many phones can read text aloud for people who find small print hard to see. It helps with long emails, signs, and books. People can change the speed, the voice, and the length of what is read at one time. They say things like "read it slower," "speak a bit quicker," or "stop after this paragraph." Others make the letters bigger by saying "make the text larger" or "I can't look at this tiny writing." Once the settings feel right, people usually leave them alone, and they only ask for a change when their eyes are tired or when the text is very long.

Marco the cook was chopping onions in a noisy kitchen when his phone buzzed. A parcel had come to the front door, but he was too busy to go. "Please tell me when the courier is near and ask him to leave the box with my neighbor," he said. The assistant understood that these were two jobs. It set an alert for the courier and wrote a change in the delivery notes: leave the parcel next door. Marco also said, "If I miss it, remind me to pick it up from the post office on Friday." The assistant said it would remind him on Friday at noon. Marco nodded and went back to his onions.

June was only six weeks old, and her mother, Dana, was new to the city and very tired. A neighbor had agreed to lend her a baby monitor, but Dana was waiting for him to knock. She grabbed her phone and typed fast, all in lowercase: "remnd me to feed june at half past two". The assistant saw the small mistake and understood the message anyway. It said it had set a reminder for two thirty to feed the baby. Then Dana typed, "and again at five". The assistant added a second reminder for five o'clock. Dana put the phone down and smiled. At last she could sit still for a minute.

Person: I'm planning a party for Saturday. Can you send out the invitations?
Assistant: Happy to. How many guests should I invite?
Person: Double the number from last year.
Assistant: Last year you invited ten people, so I will invite twenty. What time does the party start?
Person: When the moon starts to rise, around eight. The music should be perfect, not too loud.
Assistant: I will put eight o'clock on the invitations and make a quiet music list.
Person: Can you also write the names on place cards with a pen?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't write on paper. I can make a list for you to print and copy.

Nina woke up on Sunday morning with her head full of cake. It was her uncle's birthday, and she had forgotten to buy him anything. A drip from the leaking tap in the bathroom went tap, tap, tap while she rubbed her eyes. She picked up her phone and said only two words: "Gift ideas." The assistant understood that she needed a present for her uncle's birthday. It named three things: a fancy tea set, a warm scarf, and a book about boats. Nina said, "The tea set." The assistant opened a shop page and showed the price. She smiled, since the party guest list was already full and this was the last job on her list.

Sam had just moved to the city and knew nobody. After his first swim at the public pool, he sat on a bench with his phone and said, "Could you please find the audiobook I started yesterday and start it where I stopped? I want to listen on the way home, and I don't remember the chapter." The assistant understood that he wanted his last place in the book. It said, "You stopped in chapter eleven, close to the end." Then it began to play. A minute later Sam said, "Dim the screen, please, it's too bright." The assistant made the screen darker, and Sam walked home with the story in his ears.

Grandpa Walt wanted to send his granddaughter money for her birthday. She lived far away, where the winters were snowy and cold. "How many euros is fifty dollars?" he asked the tablet. Then he stopped. "No, wait, I mean sixty dollars." The assistant understood that he had changed his mind. It worked out the new amount at today's rate and said, "Sixty dollars is about fifty-five euros." Walt wanted to remember the number, so he asked the assistant to keep a note. It saved a note called "Birthday money." Then Walt said he would also buy her a paper rose, and the assistant wrote that down too.

name: top_senders
does: Lists the people who write to you most often in your inbox over a chosen time.
inputs: how many days to look back
people say:
- Who writes to me all the time?
- Show me who sent the most mail this month.
- Did my husband email me this week?
- Drop me a list of my most frequent senders.
- I'm drowning in mail, who is it from?
- Which people keep filling my inbox?

name: plan_walk_route
does: Makes a walking loop of the length you want, starting from a place you choose.
inputs: the start place, the distance, and what to avoid
people say:
- I want a short walk from the station, about two miles.
- Give me a loop that's not too hilly.
- I'm bored of the same park, find me somewhere new.
- Is there a path without snow today?
- Take me for a one hour stroll.

Priya was an office worker, and her video call was about to start. The picture kept freezing. She put one hand on her mouse and typed with the other, all in lowercase and in a hurry: "wifi so slow, can you restart the routr". The assistant understood the small typo. It said it was restarting the router and that the wifi would be back in about two minutes. Priya asked it to end the call with her friend so she could join the meeting on time. The assistant closed the call. When the router lights came back, the connection was fast again, and Priya joined the meeting with a minute to spare.

Rosa was a nurse who had just finished a night shift. It was nine in the morning, and she was too tired to think. She carried her bag through the door and the flat was cold. "Keep the heating off now, and turn it on at four this afternoon, so the rooms are warm when I wake up," she said to the thermostat. The assistant understood that she wanted to sleep without noise and then have a warm flat. It lowered the heat for several hours and set the heating to start at four. Rosa drank a glass of orange juice, put her bag on a chair, and fell asleep.

Person: How heavy is a cow?
Assistant: A grown cow weighs a lot. Do you want the weight in kilograms or in pounds?
Person: Pounds, please. Is it more than my dog?
Assistant: Yes, much more. I don't know how heavy your dog is. Can you tell me?
Person: I forgot. I think she is about fifty pounds.
Assistant: A cow is about twenty times that. It weighs around a thousand pounds.
Person: Wow. Thank you for helping me.
Assistant: You are welcome. You were very polite.

A clock tells you what time it is, and time zones tell you what time it is somewhere else. When your friend lives far away, her morning can be your evening. People use this when they schedule a call or check if someone is awake. They ask for changes with words like "show me the time in Tokyo," "what's the time at my sister's place," or "set my clock to local time." You can also get a rough idea of the time without a clock, by looking at the sun or at when the mailbox is emptied, but a phone is much easier and does not make mistakes.

Maya was a student making dinner when her hand slipped on a hot pot of beans. She had a red mark on her finger. "I think it's small," she said in a quiet voice, "but it hurts. I don't want to call an ambulance, I just want to know what to do." The assistant understood that she did not want emergency help, only advice for a small burn. It told her to hold the finger under cool running water for ten minutes and not to put on butter or ice. It also said to call for help if the skin turned white or blistered a lot. Maya followed the steps, and the pain slowly went away.

Grandma Elsa needed a new light switch for the hall. The old one had stopped working, and her grandson had helped her disconnect it. She spoke to her tablet: "Find me a plain white wall switch and have it come tomorrow at noon." The assistant found three. The first one was expensive, so it showed her a cheaper choice with the same size. "That one," said Elsa. The assistant ordered it and said it would arrive tomorrow at noon, and that she could send it back within a month. Elsa wrote the time on a card by the door and went to make tea.

Mr. Hall, a retired teacher, was expecting his grandson for the weekend. His old phone had a constant buzz of notices, and the wifi was weak. He typed quickly, all in lowercase: "make a gues network for my grandson". The assistant understood what he meant despite the typo. It set up a guest wifi with its own name and password and said that the guest network was separate from his own. Mr. Hall also asked it to ship the new router box back to the shop, since the first one was broken. The assistant started the return and said a courier would pick the box up on Monday.

They want to know how strong the sun is at the beach today.
How strong is the sun?
Do I need sun cream today?
UV level?
Will I burn if I stay out till noon?
It feels like a heater out there. Is the sun very hot?
How bad is the sun at the beach right now?
Could you please tell me how strong the sun is this afternoon, because my young daughter has pale skin and I want to know how much cream to bring?

name: feed_pet_now
does: Gives a pet one portion from the automatic feeder, and can stop it when the pet has had enough.
inputs: the pet's name and the size of the portion
people say:
- Feed Bella, please.
- Give the cat her dinner now.
- She's been in the sunshine all day, give her a snack.
- Stop the feeder, he's had enough.
- Did the dog eat the food in the bowl on the left?
- Fill up the bowl for the kitten.

They want to hear today's top news.
News?
What's happening today?
Tell me the headlines.
Read me the main stories, please.
Anything big in the news this morning?
I want an automatic summary of the top stories as soon as I wake up.
I'm waiting at the bus stop under my umbrella and have nothing to read, so could you please find the most important news from today and read it to me?

A text message is a short note that you send from your phone to another person's phone. It is useful for plans, quick questions, and little jokes. In a group chat, many people can read the same text, such as five friends planning a pizza night. People change a text before they send it, and they use words like "change the first line," "make it shorter," or "add a smiley." They also ask, "read my last text," "reply yes," or "count the total in this chat." A text should be simple, so the other person understands it fast and can answer when it suits them.

Tomas was a cook, and on Saturday he would host a big dinner. Today he was stuck in the kitchen. He had dropped his mother's necklace behind the stove, and the room was too dark to see it. "Turn on the big kitchen light, and tomorrow at seven switch it to a warm color for dinner," he said. The assistant understood. It made the ceiling light bright at once, and Tomas found the necklace. Then he asked for the robot to vacuum the floor. The assistant said it was true that the robot had not run all week, and it started it. It also set the warm light for seven tomorrow.

They want the internet connection to go faster.
The video keeps freezing.
Nothing will load.
Can you try restarting the router?
My photos won't post, the page just spins.
Less lag, please.
Everyone in the house is online and it's crawling.
I'm trying to watch a show and it takes forever to start.

Kai was a teenager sitting on the couch with his phone. His dad was outside with a hammer, fixing the frame under the new solar panels. Kai texted the home assistant: "did we use more power than last month". The assistant understood he meant the electricity use. It told him, "This month you used less, about ten percent less than last month, and the solar panels made half of your power." Kai was happy. He asked the assistant to post the numbers in the family chat. The assistant sent the message, and his mom replied with a thumbs up. Then Kai asked if the number would be double if they ran the heater all day. The assistant said it would be about double.

They want to know when the next bus comes.
Next bus?
When's the bus north?
I don't want the express, just the normal bus.
Not the five o'clock one, the one after.
The sun is shining so I'll walk to the stop, when should I leave?
I'm taking my new blender to my sister's, so when does the next bus going north come by?
Please tell me the time of the next local bus heading north, and not the train.

A video is a moving picture you record with your phone or camera. People make short clips of birthdays, trips, and their pets. A clip of a visit to the orange farm, for example, can show how the fruit hangs in the trees. After you record it, you can watch it again, make it shorter, or share it with family. People say things like "cut the first ten seconds," "send this clip to my sister," or "play it again." If someone needs a video urgently, for work or school, they often ask for it to be sent right now and in a smaller size, so it goes through quickly.

They want the latest sports scores.
Scores?
Who won the match?
How did my team do last night?
What's the score in the football game?
Who won the last round of the tennis final?
The apple pie is cooling on the counter, so while it cools could you please tell me the football score?
My friend said our team played today and I missed it. Could you please tell me the final score, since I want to know before I call him?

They want to make a recipe bigger.
Double the recipe, please.
Make it twice as much.
I need half again as much dough.
Can you make the cookies for twelve instead of six?
It's January and everyone is home, so I want to build a bigger batch than usual.
It's a quiet Sunday, but ten people are coming for cake. Can you change all the amounts so there is more for everyone?
Please scale the bread recipe up by one and a half, because I want an extra loaf to give to my neighbor.

name: night_temperature_check
does: Tells you how cold it will get at a campsite overnight, using the most recent forecast.
inputs: the campsite or place, and the date
people say:
- Will it chill down tonight in the hills?
- How cold will the tent get?
- Do I need my thick sleeping bag?
- Does the temperature fall below freezing on Saturday?
- What's the night like at the lake?

Baking turns dough or batter into bread, cake, or cookies. Heat does the work, so the time and the oven setting matter. Most recipes say to put the tray on the middle rack and to close the oven door and not open it too soon. People change how long something bakes, how warm the oven is, or how much dough they make. They say things like "bake it ten minutes longer," "make the oven hotter," or "set a timer for forty minutes." On busy days, a delivery driver may bring the flour and eggs, and the whole house smells good by evening.

Some videos are made at home with a phone, and they stay on the phone until you share them. They are for remembering things, like the kids brushing their teeth with a bright new toothbrush, or a dog that comes running when it hears the door. People change a video by cutting it, making it shorter, or turning the sound up. They say things like "trim the end," "send it to grandma," or "play my last video." A home video does not need to be perfect. What matters is that you can find it again later, so people often ask for a name to be added.

name: find_my_reservation
does: Looks up a table you booked at a restaurant and shows the time, the number of people, and the address.
inputs: the restaurant name or the date
people say:
- I lost the details of our dinner on Friday.
- Where did we book for tonight?
- What time is the table at the place on the hill?
- Do they have home delivery if we cancel?
- When is our lunch reservation?

Person: The air smells funny.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. Which room are you in?
Person: The kitchen. The oven was on a long time.
Assistant: Thank you. Do you want me to scan the air in the kitchen?
Person: Yes, please. It's late and I'm a little scared.
Assistant: The air in the kitchen is not good. The score is twenty-five out of one hundred. Please open the window and ask a grown-up to turn off the oven.
Person: Okay. Can you open the window for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't open windows. But I can turn on the fan.

name: set_bedtime_alarm
does: Sets a gentle alarm for waking up and a reminder for going to bed, based on how much sleep you want.
inputs: the wake-up time and the hours of sleep
people say:
- Wake me at six thirty tomorrow.
- I want eight hours of sleep, when should I go to bed?
- Add ten more minutes, I'm so tired.
- Remind the whole family to go to bed at nine.
- My little girl needs a tiny nap before dinner, wake her in half an hour.

A world clock shows the time in other places at once. It is useful when you want to report in to a boss far away, or when you listen to a live podcast that starts at a certain hour in another country. People keep a personal list of the cities they care about, such as where family lives. They change the list when they need to, with words like "show me the time in Lima," "put Paris on my clock," or "take Rome off." Some also ask, "is it too late to call my brother?" and the clock tells them if it is night there.

They want more packing boxes for moving.
I need more boxes.
Get me ten medium boxes.
Order twice as many as last time.
I ran out of boxes, can you send half a dozen more?
Can you teach me how many boxes a small flat needs, then order that many?
One extra large box for the lamp and another for my phone charger and cables, please.
Could you please order twenty more medium boxes for the move on Friday, because we have more books than I thought?

Email is a way to send letters over the internet. You write a message, add a name and a subject, and press send. People use it for work, bills, and plans, like a trip with friends. The inbox holds mail you get, and the unread mail is in bold. People ask for changes with words like "mark all as read," "reply to the last email," or "text me when the boss writes." A big attachment or a very long email can be expensive for slow connections, so many people send a small photo and a short note instead. They ask, "make it shorter."

They want to reserve a hotel room for two nights.
Book me a room for two nights.
I need somewhere to sleep near the train station.
A room for two on Friday and Saturday, please.
Find me a room with a nice design and book it, and tell me if breakfast is cooked fresh.
Can you find a quiet hotel for two people next weekend and check what time we can get in?
I'm coming to town with my wife, so please book a double room for the night of the tenth and send me the address.

They want to know how much money is worth in another currency.
How much is fifty euros in dollars?
What's the pound rate?
Dollars to yen right now?
I have a fever, so I can't go to the bank. What will the rate be tomorrow at nine?
I'm looking forward to my trip. Is the Mexican peso going up or down?
Are my euros ready to buy something that costs two hundred dollars?
Could you please tell me what a hundred pounds will be in euros tomorrow at nine in the morning, because I want to change my money then?

name: scale_recipe
does: Changes the amounts in a recipe so it makes more or fewer servings.
inputs: the recipe and the number of servings you want
people say:
- Make this soup for six instead of two.
- My partner is coming, so double the pasta.
- Cut the cake recipe in half.
- Walk me through how much flour I need for twelve cookies.
- I want this to be tasty for a crowd, make it for twenty.

name: move_between_my_accounts
does: Moves money from one of your own accounts to another.
inputs: which account to take from, which to put into, and how much
people say:
- Put fifty dollars into my savings.
- I'm saving up for swim lessons, set some money aside.
- Return the money I took from my holiday account.
- Every month, send twenty pounds to my other account.
- Take a hundred out of checking and put it in my rainy day account.

Mrs. Green was a retired teacher, and she did not like to rush. She sat in the kitchen with her phone while dinner was cooked on the stove. "Would you be so kind as to move two hundred dollars from my checking to my savings?" she said. "I want to be sure the rent is safe before the month ends, and I always forget." The assistant understood that she wanted a transfer between her own accounts. It asked her to confirm the amount, and she did. Then it said the money was moved and read her the new balances. She asked it to change the setting so it would warn her when her checking was low. The assistant said it would, and she smiled. "I guess that's all."

name: pack_list_check
does: Goes through your packing list and tells you what you have not packed yet for a hike or a night out.
inputs: the trip type and the length in days
people say:
- Did I forget anything for the weekend?
- Scan my list for a two day hike.
- Do I have enough for half the trail?
- We have a wide river to cross, what else do I need?
- What's missing from my bag?

Jonas was an office worker with a long day. He said to his calendar assistant, "Put the team meeting on Tuesday at two." The assistant did. Then Jonas looked at his mug of stale coffee and said, "No, sorry, make it Wednesday, not Tuesday." The assistant moved the meeting to Wednesday at two and said so plainly. Jonas also needed to upload the slides before the meeting, so he asked for a reminder. The assistant set one for Wednesday at one. Jonas had to plug in his laptop, because the battery was low, and he got back to work. The calendar now showed only the new time.

Omar was a driver and he was hungry after a long drive. He pulled over and said, "Order me a pepperoni pizza from Luigi's, to come on Wednesday evening." The assistant began the order. Then Omar thought about his flat tire, and the long wait for a tow truck, and he said, "No, make that a mushroom pizza, and I want it tonight, not Wednesday." The assistant understood the correction. It changed the pizza to mushroom, changed the day to tonight, and said the food would arrive in thirty minutes. Omar also asked for a tip of three dollars for the rider. The assistant added it, and Omar sat back to wait.

Zoe, a teenager, was in a group chat with her friends. They were planning a surprise party for Mia, and Zoe had to be careful. She picked up her phone and said, "Write to the group, and don't mention Mia, because it's a secret." The assistant wrote, "Let's celebrate on Saturday at four, bring cake," and did not use the name Mia. Then Zoe said, "Don't send it yet. Read it to me first." The assistant read the message out loud. Zoe liked it, and said to send it. Later she scrolled to the bottom of the chat and saw her friends' answers. She wrote down the plan on a napkin, too.
